programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Otto a feuchainn ri toirt air Oona gun a bhith cho eagallach mun dorchadas 's e ga brosnachadh a dhol chun na traghad le fhèin... tron oidhche! Otto attempts to help Oona get over a fear of the dark by encouraging her to take a special trip to the beach by herself... a night-time trip!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha i air a bhith sileadh gu trom air a chreag 's a-nis tha poll anns gach àit'! Tha Mama airson 's gun cùm Oona sùil air Baba 's gun cùm i glan e - obair dhùbhlanach 's Baba airson leum 's na loin 's coimhead sna lochain! It has been raining heavily on the rock and now there's mud everywhere. Mama has asked Oona to watch Baba and to keep him nice and clean - a big challenge, as Baba wants to jump in muddy puddles and investigate the pond life.

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Tha Boban air bhioran an-diugh - oir tha prèasant còmhdaicht’ aige do dh’ Fhuigheag! Ach an dùil a bheil fios aig Fuigheag dè th’ ann am prèasant? Boban is excited today, as he has a wrapped present for Fuigheag! Does Fuigheag know what a present is though?

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Tha Sif, Pipp agus Bran a’ cleachdadh foidhle gus long-fhànais a chruthachadh. Ziff, Pipp and Button use kitchen foil to create and launch an out-of-this-world spaceship.

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: An-diugh tha Pàdraig agus Heidi còmhla rithe ‘s iad a’ dèanamh coiridh ghlasrach. Ach mus tòisich iad, feumaidh iad a bhith cinnteach gu bheil an stuth a tha a dhìth orra a-staigh. Mur a bheil, bidh iad a’ dèanamh liosta agus a’ dol dhan bhùth airson a h-uile càil fhaighinn. Bidh Linda agus a caraidean cuideachd a’ faighinn a-mach mar a thathar a’ fàs càl-colaig. Tha iad an uairsin a’ tilleadh dhan chidsin airson a’ choiridh ullachadh mus suidh iad sìos aig a’ bhòrd ga ithe. Linda is joined by Patrick and Heidi to make vegetable curry. Before cooking, they have to ensure all the ingredients are present. If not, they make a list and go shopping for what's missing. They also learn more about how cauliflowers are grown, then return to the kitchen to make the curry before sitting down to tuck in.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Gillebrìde Mac ’IlleMhaoil a’ leughadh Am Prionnsa Beag. Tha an sgeulachd stèidhte air an nobhail aig Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, leasaichte le Louise Greig, dealbhaichte le Sarah Massinni agus air eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Gillebrìde Mac 'IlleMhaoil. Gillebrìde MacMillan reads Am Prionnsa Beag. The story is based on the novel by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, adapted by Louise Greig, illustrated by Sarah Massinni and translated into Gaelic by Gillebrìde MacMillan.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Tha aig a' chlann ri diofar pheataichean a thoirt leotha dhan sgoil an-diugh oir ‘s e Là Bi-iomadachd a th’ann. Tha Stella feumach air taic – saoil an tèid Mgr. P ann còmhla rithe? The children have to take different pets to school as it’s Biodiversity Day. Stella needs help, but will Mgr P go with her?

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Tha an dealbh Rìoghail dol a bhith air a thogail a-nochd ach, gu mì-fhortanach, tha cùisean air a dhol ceàrr le Stella. Tha trioblaid dathadh-fuilt ag adhbharachadh gu bheil falt Stella air a mhilleadh. Dè chanas an Rìgh 's a' Bhànrigh? The Royal portrait is being taken tonight but, unfortunately, things have gone awry for Stella. A dye incident has meant that her hair is ruined. What will the King and Queen say?

programme.title: A’ Chùil
programme.desc: Tha Choirstaidh air ais le prògram eile bhon stiùidio aice, A’ Chùil. Sa phrògram seo seallaidh i dhut dòigh sgoinneil air coltas eadar-dhealaichte a thoirt air do chuid aodaich! Choirstaidh presents from her studio A’ Chùil to show you a great way of changing up your clothes.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Tha sinn air ais ann an Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche airson teirm ùr. Tha tòrr air tachairt thairis air na saor-làithean. Cha robh an là in-sheirbheis cho soirbheachail `s a bha Maighstir Mackle an dùil agus tha Ms Sharpe air nochdadh sna pàipearan-naidheachd ri linn ‘s na thachair aig a’ Mhòd. Our cameras are back at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche for a new term. A lot has happened over the holidays. The in-service day wasn’t as successful as Mr Mackle had hoped and Ms Sharpe has made the newspapers after what happened at the Mòd.

programme.title: The Deep/An Doimhne
programme.desc: Dè tha Alpheus Benthos ris an-diugh? As bith dè, chan eil smachd aige air gnothaichean! What is Alpheus Benthos up to today? Whatever it is, he has no control over things!

programme.title: Dùbhlain DIY (Instructions Not Included)
programme.desc: Derek 'Pluto' Murray hosts a fun knockout amateur DIY competition where couples go head to head. Derek 'Pluto' Moireach le farpais spòrsail DIY is cupail a’ strì an aghaidh a chèile.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: We meet learner Keith Mackenzie from the Isle of Skye and Calum Maclean is in Argyll, on the hunt for one of Scotland’s more reclusive creatures.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc: Ramsay meets writer and producer Maureen MacLeod just north of Glasgow to enjoy the nature right on their doorstep. The pair follow the popular West Highland Way route as Maureen talks about the importance of home and how that has shaped her career. She opens up about her passion for travel and visiting new places, but also the tough reality of travelling to hostile environments. Tha Ramsay MacMahon air ais leis an dàrna sreath de Rathad Ramsay, far a bheil e a’ coinneachadh ri Gàidheil aithnichte air feadh na dùthcha airson cuairt, còmhradh agus cnuasachadh. Tha Ramsay a’ coinneachadh ris an sgrìobhadair agus an riochdaire, Maureen NicLeòid, dìreach tuath air Glaschu gus an rud as fheàrr a dhèanamh dhen nàdar air an starsaich. Tha an dithis a’ leantainn Slighe na Gàidhealtachd an Iar fhad ’s a tha Maureen a’ bruidhinn mu cho cudromach ’s a tha a dachaigh dhi agus mar a thug e buaidh air a cuid obrach. Tha i ag innse mun ùidh mhòr a th’ aice ann a bhith a’ siubhal agus a’ tadhal air àiteachan ùra, ach cuideachd mu cho doirbh ’s a tha e a bhith a’ siubhal gu sgìrean nàimhdeil. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc: Tha Màiri Ross ag ionnsachadh mu eich dùthchasach na h-Alba. Mairi Ross learns about Scotland’s native horses.

programme.title: Port
programme.desc: Music documentary in which Julie Fowlis and Muireann NicAmhlaoibh explore shared musical roots in Donegal.

programme.title: Greenland: Sgeul Isobel Wylie Hutchison
programme.desc: Kirsty MacDonald follows in the footsteps of pioneering Scottish adventurer Isobel Wylie Hutchison.

programme.title: Glan Fhèin
programme.desc: Tha na seann charaidean Katie agus Angela a’ stiùireadh companaidh glanaidh a bhios a’ seirbhiseachadh thaighean air mhàl geàrr-ùine gu h-àraidh. Tha an gnìomhachas air leth soirbheachail agus tha sùil aig Lewis Friseal, a tha na entrepreneur ionadail agus na chomhairliche spèiseail, anns a’ chompanaidh. Aig an aon àm, tha Betty a’ taisbeanadh bàrdachd a tha brosnaichte le peataichean agus i a’ gabhail ri call pearsanta. Le Dido a’ dèanamh air an ospadal gus leanabh a bhreith, tha Daniel a’ dèanamh beagan matamataig air leatromachd leantaileach. An dàrna sreath den sit-com fhèillmhor le Hannah McKirdy agus Lana Pheutan mar chleasaichean agus sgrìobhaichean. Old pals Katie and Angela run a cleaning company that specialises in servicing short-term lets. Business is booming and local entrepreneur and esteemed councillor Lewis Fraser has the company in his sights. Meanwhile, Betty performs pet-inspired poetry as she comes to terms with a personal loss. As Dido rushes to the hospital to give birth, Daniel does the maths on extended long-term pregnancy. Second series of the hit sitcom written by and starring Hannah McKirdy and Lana Pheutan. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Looking at the secret lives of the wildlife in one of Britain's favourite gardens. Shot by Charlie Hamilton-James, this film follows various animals, from the family of foxes that play after hours in the pleasure gardens to the toads in the Italian garden and the badgers that clear up the tea rooms at night. Set against the background of the gardening year, these stories reveal life behind the scenes at Heligan.

programme.title: Inside Classical
programme.desc: The BBC Philharmonic Orchestra, led by Ludovic Morlot, presents a concert celebrating spring’s extraordinary creative power as a season of renewal and rebirth, through evocative lighting and musical soundscapes, from Manchester’s Aviva Studios. Presented by Ben Gernon. Igor Stravinsky’s ballet score The Rite of Spring, which famously incited audience uproar in its 1913 Paris premiere, is an exhilarating start to the programme. With its asymmetrical rhythms, brutal harmonies and sonic aggression, it continues to fascinate audiences today and remains one of the most influential works of the 20th century. The UK premiere of Jessie Montgomery’s Chemiluminescence follows in calm contrast. This work for string orchestra introduces an atmosphere of contemplative beauty as science and the natural world are united through sound in the composer’s musical depiction of the creation of light from a non-light source. An evocative programme of musical concepts, exploring spring’s explosive destruction and radiant light.

programme.desc: Concert featuring Indian musician Ravi Shankar, first shown in 1974. He performs just one song, entitled Rag Behag.

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: It’s the grand final of the series. Of the 28 teams that started the tournament, only two remain - but which will lift the trophy? Jeremy Paxman asks the questions.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take you so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. In the second semi-final, three fans of the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy lock horns with the cunning of the Strategists, a team bound by their love of obscure European board games. They'll compete to draw together the connections between elements which at first glance seem utterly random.

programme.title: This World
programme.desc: Adventurer and journalist Simon Reeve heads to east Africa to uncover the stories behind the nation's favourite drink. While we drink millions of cups of the stuff each day, how many of us know where our tea actually comes from? The surprising answer is that most of the leaves that go into our everyday teabags do not come from India or China but are bought from an auction in the coastal city of Mombasa in Kenya. From here, Simon follows the tea trail through the epic landscapes of Kenya and Uganda and meets some of the millions of people who pick, pack and transport our tea. Drinking tea with everyone from Masai cattle herders to the descendants of the original white tea planters, Simon learns that the industry that supplies our everyday cuppa is not immune to the troubles of the continent - poverty, low wages and child labour.

programme.title: Andy Warhol's America
programme.desc: Charting Andy Warhol's response to the civil rights movement and the assassination of John F Kennedy, as well as other major historical events happening in America in the 1960s. We hear stories about Warhol setting up the Silver Factory and managing The Velvet Underground, and also how he faced his own personal nightmare: he was shot by a Factory associate.

programme.title: American Visions
programme.desc: Robert Hughes examines America's development into the art capital of the west between 1945 and the late 1960s, with the advent of abstract expressionism and pop art.

programme.title: imagine...
programme.desc: Twenty-something virtuoso multi-instrumentalist, singer and arranger Jacob Collier has managed to outdo The Beatles by winning Grammy Awards for each of his first four albums. Alan Yentob meets Jacob and musicians he has collaborated with, including Stormzy, Chris Martin and film composer Hans Zimmer. He also talks to music legends Quincy Jones and Herbie Hancock, who believe Jacob Collier is one of the most talented musicians on the planet today.

programme.title: Stolen: Catching the Art Thieves
programme.desc: The astonishing story of the theft of two Turners on loan from the Tate in 1994 sparking a high-stakes international hunt across Europe from London to Belgrade, deep into the world of Serbian war lords.

programme.title: Talking Movies
programme.desc: To mark America's 250th anniversary, Talking Movies hears from leading figures in US media, film and culture who tell the BBC about some iconic American movies and what these films reveal about the country and the psyche of her people. American Psycho director Mary Harron talks about Martin Scorsese's The King of Comedy, while critic and film-maker Bilge Ebiri looks at Hitchcock's classic thriller North by Northwest. BBC News presenter Sumi Somaskanda reveals her passion for the prison drama The Shawshank Redemption and award-winning journalist Tim Teeman selects Steven Spielberg's Jaws. Talking Movies' host Tom Brook chooses the Robert Altman ensemble satire Nashville. Each contributor speaks about what their film choice means to them and how and why they feel it has become an American cinema classic. This special illustrates the American nation on the big screen and the influence it's had in bringing its movies to the world.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Imagine a warehouse bigger than a football pitch, full of some of science’s most important items. Near Swindon, Christina Trevanion visits the Science and Innovation Park to see some of the 400,000 objects stored there on behalf of England’s science museums. Among the most treasured items are personal possessions from the office of the late Professor Stephen Hawking, including a wheelchair, his specially adapted glasses and a figurine of his Simpsons character. Hoping for a breakthrough of their own are two teams of friends and colleagues browsing a bustling antiques fair in Exeter. In red are Vickie and Hannah, activities coordinators at the same care home, who watch the show every day with their residents! In blue are palliative care nurses Lindsay and Sarah, who both admit to being mad about dogs. With expert Ben Cooper in tow, the reds steer a course for a ship’s wheel, but Captain Cooper isn’t impressed with the high price. The blues alongside Gary Pe are true to their word, sidetracked by an art-deco-style dog statue and then distracted by the real thing in the arms of its owner!

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Imagine a warehouse bigger than a football pitch, full of some of science’s most important items. Near Swindon, Christina Trevanion visits the Science and Innovation Park to see some of the 400,000 objects stored there on behalf of England’s science museums. Among the most treasured items are personal possessions from the office of the late Professor Stephen Hawking, including a wheelchair, his specially adapted glasses and a figurine of his Simpsons character. Hoping for a breakthrough of their own are two teams of friends and colleagues browsing a bustling antiques fair in Exeter. In red are Vickie and Hannah, activities coordinators at the same care home, who watch the show every day with their residents! In blue are palliative care nurses Lindsay and Sarah, who both admit to being mad about dogs. With expert Ben Cooper in tow, the reds steer a course for a ship’s wheel, but Captain Cooper isn’t impressed with the high price. The blues alongside Gary Pe are true to their word, sidetracked by an art-deco-style dog statue and then distracted by the real thing in the arms of its owner!

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: The Great Food Guys
programme.desc: Chef Nick Nairn and Dougie Vipond are on a mission to highlight the fantastic range of great produce Scotland has to offer. This week they’re looking at beef, cooking an Aberdeen Angus fillet steak cache with a green peppercorn sauce and creamed spinach. Joining them in the kitchen are Fife buffalo farmer Steve Mitchell and food and drink writer Gabriella Bennett, who has chosen a spicy beer from the Borders to accompany the beef.

programme.title: The River
programme.desc: It's common riding fever along the River Tweed and that means a lot of work for farrier David Merry and his apprentice Ross. In this episode, David has the small task of seeing to all the horses at the Jedburgh common ride and the larger task of rescuing his van. Former Galashiels braw lass and horse racing trainer Katie Scott is preparing horses for the gala rideout along with travelling draper Richard Mackay. Richard's daughter Alice is the 'bearer of the white roses', and Katie faces a former Grand National winner in a chase to the top of the hill. Across River Tweed tributaries, biologist James Hunt is 'electro-fishing' to find evidence that the salmon and trout spawning grounds have survived the winter floods. After six long months, Ruth Hinks finally launches her new chocolate school with a royal twist. At Floors Stud, manager David Trouton is overseeing one of the most important days of the year, their young horses are getting shod for the first time with a little help from farrier David Merry, and on Cowbog Farm, Robert Wilson is checking on the young calves, trying to select his best of the herd for the Kelso show with daughter Lottie.

programme.title: The River
programme.desc: The final episode of The River, and summer is coming to an end with a bang. The Floors Stud team prepare for the most important day of their year, the sales at Newmarket. But before they can get to the sales, the horses need conditioning so some lunge training is required. In Peebles, Fiona and Neil Dalgleish organise the International Enduro at Glentress Forest, where international pro riders will hit some of the valley's steepest and fastest trails, this being the biggest event of its kind in Britain. On the river, ghillie Colin Bell strims more grassy riverbanks and sees to his summer fishing clients, and on Cowbog Farm, Lottie blowdries her dad's prized Hereford herd. With cows chosen for the show, Lottie and dad Robert will be aiming high come show day. Finally, it's judgement day for the Floors Stud team, they make it to the Tattersalls auction with their best six horses, 12 months of dedication and hard graft will come down to just a few minutes in the sales ring. The pressure is on.

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: Alan Carr kicks off the competition by tasking ten interior designers to show off their signature styles by transforming a beach hut on the Dorset coast. They must also demonstrate their ability to reuse and repurpose where they can. Michelle Ogundehin and guest judge Jonathan Adler must decide who has created the Stand Out Space and which designer will be the first to go home.

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: A determined DCI Douglas is in the trenches interrogating Harry when he is stunned to receive new evidence, and a bitter Caitlin takes action when Scarlett and Sam return from Nashville. Meanwhile, Jodie teaches an obnoxious Callum and Shak a lesson, and Gillian is concerned over Mikey’s response to the press.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Over at Alan and Michelle’s, Alan’s bullying big brother Michael turns up to sort the rings for his wedding. Meanwhile, Christine catches Michelle on the street and persuades them to come over to Beth’s so they can get a look at the groom. Christine goes on about how handsome and funny Michael is while managing to make everyone else feel inadequate. Especially Alan. With the rings to keep safe, a list of chores to do and Colin showing off his sexy stripper moves, the gathering soon descends into chaos. He may be the best man, but it turns out nobody really has any confidence in Alan’s abilities to do anything other than order two puddings at the meal – let alone make a speech.

programme.title: The Chief
programme.desc: Though he is married to the force, and justice is his mistress, the Chief feels the time is right to dip his toe into the water and get back out there, hoping to meet a high-flyer at a similar level to himself.

programme.title: Janey and Ashley Get a Real Job
programme.desc: Ashley and Janey try their hand at various jobs in a factory that produces everything from hand lotion to shower gel, and soap to candles. They are pushed on their ability to follow instructions and complete repetitive tasks. From restocking the on-site shop, to making soap and filling bottles, everything must be uniform and be produced at speed, with very little room for error. Trying to keep their minds from wandering, and the mess to a minimum, Ashley and Janey are put through their paces by a boss who has no time for fooling around. Janey is determined to win, but she can’t stop her creativity from taking over when she should be following a precise shop display. programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Nick and Derek get some bad news, putting plans for taking over the family farm into sharp focus in Dumfries and Galloway. They are losing 300 acres of leased grazing land to forestry, and with concerns over when dad Derek might retire, Nick sets out a timeline for his succession. On Papa Westray, new farmers Paul and Mel are in the midst of their first big lambing season. With the addition of new baby Oak, it’s a family affair. Ten-year-old Jakey does the morning rounds, checking for new lambs, and spots a ewe in trouble - Paul has to call on his farming neighbours for help. At Hillhead Farm near Glasgow, Ben and Matt Imrie are tackling the wedding and events site infrastructure. The race is on to make it a marketable venue ahead of the first event of the season in six weeks' time. Their dad, John, has another pre-op for his hip replacement, and he and Antoinette hope he receives the news he is desperately waiting for.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Lizzie Schofield and Brian Cunningham are starting new projects and checking on the progress of planting carried out in previous years. Lizzie is in her herb garden, which she renovated in 2024, assessing what has worked and what needs to be refreshed. Meanwhile, Brian is checking on the apple trees he planted in the spring as examples of espalier shaping and pruning. Lizzie begins plans in the garden for cut flowers that will give her foliage alongside the blooms already beginning to take shape, and Brian is planting more perennials in the terraced patio area. There are all the usual handy hints, as well as a look at what plants are good for attracting birds to your plot.

programme.title: This is BBC Scotland
programme.desc: Highlights from the BBC Scotland channel.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: The Great Food Guys
programme.desc: Chef Nick Nairn and Dougie Vipond are on a mission to highlight the fantastic range of great produce Scotland has to offer. This week they’re looking at beef, cooking an Aberdeen Angus fillet steak cache with a green peppercorn sauce and creamed spinach. Joining them in the kitchen are Fife buffalo farmer Steve Mitchell and food and drink writer Gabriella Bennett, who has chosen a spicy beer from the Borders to accompany the beef.

programme.title: The River
programme.desc: It's common riding fever along the River Tweed and that means a lot of work for farrier David Merry and his apprentice Ross. In this episode, David has the small task of seeing to all the horses at the Jedburgh common ride and the larger task of rescuing his van. Former Galashiels braw lass and horse racing trainer Katie Scott is preparing horses for the gala rideout along with travelling draper Richard Mackay. Richard's daughter Alice is the 'bearer of the white roses', and Katie faces a former Grand National winner in a chase to the top of the hill. Across River Tweed tributaries, biologist James Hunt is 'electro-fishing' to find evidence that the salmon and trout spawning grounds have survived the winter floods. After six long months, Ruth Hinks finally launches her new chocolate school with a royal twist. At Floors Stud, manager David Trouton is overseeing one of the most important days of the year, their young horses are getting shod for the first time with a little help from farrier David Merry, and on Cowbog Farm, Robert Wilson is checking on the young calves, trying to select his best of the herd for the Kelso show with daughter Lottie.

programme.title: The River
programme.desc: The final episode of The River, and summer is coming to an end with a bang. The Floors Stud team prepare for the most important day of their year, the sales at Newmarket. But before they can get to the sales, the horses need conditioning so some lunge training is required. In Peebles, Fiona and Neil Dalgleish organise the International Enduro at Glentress Forest, where international pro riders will hit some of the valley's steepest and fastest trails, this being the biggest event of its kind in Britain. On the river, ghillie Colin Bell strims more grassy riverbanks and sees to his summer fishing clients, and on Cowbog Farm, Lottie blowdries her dad's prized Hereford herd. With cows chosen for the show, Lottie and dad Robert will be aiming high come show day. Finally, it's judgement day for the Floors Stud team, they make it to the Tattersalls auction with their best six horses, 12 months of dedication and hard graft will come down to just a few minutes in the sales ring. The pressure is on.

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: Alan Carr kicks off the competition by tasking ten interior designers to show off their signature styles by transforming a beach hut on the Dorset coast. They must also demonstrate their ability to reuse and repurpose where they can. Michelle Ogundehin and guest judge Jonathan Adler must decide who has created the Stand Out Space and which designer will be the first to go home.

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: A determined DCI Douglas is in the trenches interrogating Harry when he is stunned to receive new evidence, and a bitter Caitlin takes action when Scarlett and Sam return from Nashville. Meanwhile, Jodie teaches an obnoxious Callum and Shak a lesson, and Gillian is concerned over Mikey’s response to the press.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Over at Alan and Michelle’s, Alan’s bullying big brother Michael turns up to sort the rings for his wedding. Meanwhile, Christine catches Michelle on the street and persuades them to come over to Beth’s so they can get a look at the groom. Christine goes on about how handsome and funny Michael is while managing to make everyone else feel inadequate. Especially Alan. With the rings to keep safe, a list of chores to do and Colin showing off his sexy stripper moves, the gathering soon descends into chaos. He may be the best man, but it turns out nobody really has any confidence in Alan’s abilities to do anything other than order two puddings at the meal – let alone make a speech.

programme.title: The Chief
programme.desc: Though he is married to the force, and justice is his mistress, the Chief feels the time is right to dip his toe into the water and get back out there, hoping to meet a high-flyer at a similar level to himself.

programme.title: Janey and Ashley Get a Real Job
programme.desc: Ashley and Janey try their hand at various jobs in a factory that produces everything from hand lotion to shower gel, and soap to candles. They are pushed on their ability to follow instructions and complete repetitive tasks. From restocking the on-site shop, to making soap and filling bottles, everything must be uniform and be produced at speed, with very little room for error. Trying to keep their minds from wandering, and the mess to a minimum, Ashley and Janey are put through their paces by a boss who has no time for fooling around. Janey is determined to win, but she can’t stop her creativity from taking over when she should be following a precise shop display. The question is, will it land her the ‘best employee’ trophy, or that one last job that nobody wants to do?

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Wildlife expert Steve Backshall meets one of the planet's ultimate killers, the saltwater crocodile, as the Deadly 60 team land in Australia's Northern Territories. A rogue croc is terrorising local fisherman, so it is time to lend the park rangers a hand in catching and relocating this prehistoric monster. Steve heads deep into an abandoned mine on a ghost hunt. He is on the search for ghost bats, awesome creatures with huge fangs, that drop on to their prey out of the night sky. Scary stuff, and a first for the Deadly team as these bats have never been filmed in the wild before.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Honey attempts to clear Billy’s name. Kim continues to avoid Denise out of guilt.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May set out to end the chaos and misery that snowfall brings to Britain every year, using a combine harvester, some basic engineering skills and a quick trip to Norway. Jeremy is on the test track in the Audi RS5 and the BMW M3, and there's a rather surprising guest in the Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: The Beauty Queen and the Catfish
programme.desc: Dr David Graham is online and looking for love. He seems to have it all: the looks, the job, and the charisma. On paper, he’s Kilmarnock’s most eligible bachelor. But when the town’s former beauty queen Abbie Draper starts to receive messages from him after he treats her grandfather in hospital, she gets the feeling he might be too good to be true. She turns online sleuth and starts to uncover a trail of deception, crazy coincidences and stories that just don’t add up. Dr David isn’t just a bad boyfriend; something more sinister is afoot. Abbie starts trying to figure out who David Graham really is and why he is doing this.

programme.title: The Beauty Queen and the Catfish
programme.desc: Dr David’s victims begin comparing their stories, and it becomes clear they are dealing with a sophisticated catfish. But nothing could prepare them for the shocking truth of the perpetrator’s true identity, which leaves the women with more questions than answers. But when beauty queen Abbie takes these findings to the police, they are unable to do anything about it, and the Catfish of Kilmarnock remains free to target more and more victims. Abbie can’t walk away, and steps up her investigation over months that turn into years. As she continues to track the catfish, the scale of their criminality comes into focus, with victims spread across the country and dating back over a decade. This is one of the UK’s most prolific ever catfish, and they are not done yet.

programme.title: The Beauty Queen and the Catfish
programme.desc: As criminal investigations take hold, the victims finally have justice, but they are still left urgently searching for answers as they try to rebuild their lives. What drives someone, with a seemingly normal life, to throw it all away to terrorise countless women from the same town? With no clear motive and no explanation from the person in the frame, this very modern true crime tale now turns to those closest to the perpetrator, who are also trying to understand the mystery behind the repeated cycles of offending. As the beauty queen and the catfish’s lives become ever more entangled, lines begin to blur, loyalties are tested, and Abbie finds herself questioning everything as history repeats, and the moral complexity of crime and punishment in the internet age is laid bare. For the many victims, the question remains: what drives someone to become one of the UK’s most prolific catfish - and why can’t they stop?

programme.title: Teen Predator/Online Killer
programme.desc: Twenty-year-old Alexander McCartney, already known to police, is arrested and his devices seized after a 12-year-old girl in Scotland reports a serious catfishing abuse incident online. McCartney gives a ‘no comment’ interview while in custody, and without enough physical evidence to charge him, he is released on bail. Back home at his parents’ house, McCartney’s bail conditions are supposed to prevent him from using devices that can connect to the internet. Meanwhile, a second report comes in to the police about another catfishing abuse victim linked to online activity from McCartney’s home address. This time, it involves a young girl in New Zealand. As the police continue to gather up enough physical evidence to charge McCartney, the Cyber Crime Centre completes the analysis of one of his devices, revealing a prolific online predator at a scale never before seen by police in Northern Ireland.

programme.title: Teen Predator/Online Killer
programme.desc: With hundreds of thousands of images of child abuse discovered on McCartney’s devices, the race is on to get him remanded into custody. McCartney is rearrested in the early hours of the morning, at which time police discover McCartney’s phone on his bedside table, where his final victim was abused on Snapchat just hours before. The US Department of Homeland Security notify the police in Northern Ireland of two more catfishing victims, this time in the United States, and a multiagency international investigation is triggered. As McCartney is remanded into custody, police across the world work together to identify and safeguard the thousands of victims discovered on McCartney’s devices. Police are especially keen to identify and locate a 14-year-old girl in Oregon, whose images McCartney used to catfish hundreds of other children. With McCartney due in court to plead guilty to charges of making indecent of images of children and blackmail, the case takes a different turn when Homeland Security finds an obituary page for Cimarron Thomas, one of his victims in West Virginia.

programme.title: Teen Predator/Online Killer
programme.desc: As police piece together the last few minutes of Cimarron’s life, they realise McCartney was still online threatening her when she tragically shot herself. Police and prosecutors move quickly to establish if there’s a case for manslaughter. Police from Northern Ireland travel to West Virginia to conduct the manslaughter investigation, where they learn that Cimarron’s own family had no idea why she took her own life. In a tragic turn, they learn that 18 months after her death, Cimarron’s father had also died by suicide. In order to charge McCartney with manslaughter, the police have to prove that he foresaw the risk to her life. As they comb through the cyber evidence from his devices, they build a case for manslaughter and charge him. The case sets new legal precedent in the UK. More than five years after the police investigation began, McCartney is finally convicted and sentenced.

programme.title: Liar: The Fake Grooming Scandal
programme.desc: Twenty-two-year-old Ellie Williams was jailed for lying about being trafficked and raped by a vicious Asian grooming gang. Now, for the first time, the truth is laid open.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Charlie Ross uncorks an episode of the show fizzing with fun and excitement at the South of England Showground in West Sussex. Among the stalls at Ardingly Antiques Fair, he quizzes punters about a mystery metal object. While they ponder its purpose, two teams of antiques hunters search for three profitable items to take to auction. On the red team are friends Alex and Ollie, skippered by expert Jonathan Pratt. Against them are the blues, pals Lesley and Rachel, who are shopping with expert Kate Bliss. Early in their shop, Kate spots a silk handbag that looks as if it's art deco but on closer inspection is revealed to be something later, so it goes back in the cabinet. Over with the reds, the lads spy an Edwardian desk set, but Jonathan doesn’t think it’s very practical, so it fails to make the grade. With minutes left on the clock, one team relaxes with a cake and a cuppa, while the other rushes to bag their last buy. In Buckinghamshire, auctioneer Hugo Lemon is ready and waiting to sell the teams’ items, but can he hammer out profits for either of them?

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob travel to Mid Wales to fish for wild carp in some equally wild and wonderfully picturesque lake locations. They've had success catching both mirror and common carp in previous trips, but trying to net a ‘Welsh wildie’ will require a different approach. Wild carp are the oldest strain of the species we have in the UK, and there are tales from the middle ages of monks tending carp ponds. Starting off high in the Welsh hills, Paul and Bob spend their first day fishing an ancient glacial lake. Bob has some new carp gear that he is keen to use and hopes will make a difference to his fishing. During this trip, Bob and Paul also meet Mick May and Marina Gibson, who together have started a charity called Cancer and Pisces, which offers fishing as therapeutic respite for people with cancer.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Charlie Ross uncorks an episode of the show fizzing with fun and excitement at the South of England Showground in West Sussex. Among the stalls at Ardingly Antiques Fair, he quizzes punters about a mystery metal object. While they ponder its purpose, two teams of antiques hunters search for three profitable items to take to auction. On the red team are friends Alex and Ollie, skippered by expert Jonathan Pratt. Against them are the blues, pals Lesley and Rachel, who are shopping with expert Kate Bliss. Early in their shop, Kate spots a silk handbag that looks as if it's art deco but on closer inspection is revealed to be something later, so it goes back in the cabinet. Over with the reds, the lads spy an Edwardian desk set, but Jonathan doesn’t think it’s very practical, so it fails to make the grade. With minutes left on the clock, one team relaxes with a cake and a cuppa, while the other rushes to bag their last buy. In Buckinghamshire, auctioneer Hugo Lemon is ready and waiting to sell the teams’ items, but can he hammer out profits for either of them?

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob travel to Mid Wales to fish for wild carp in some equally wild and wonderfully picturesque lake locations. They've had success catching both mirror and common carp in previous trips, but trying to net a ‘Welsh wildie’ will require a different approach. Wild carp are the oldest strain of the species we have in the UK, and there are tales from the middle ages of monks tending carp ponds. Starting off high in the Welsh hills, Paul and Bob spend their first day fishing an ancient glacial lake. Bob has some new carp gear that he is keen to use and hopes will make a difference to his fishing. During this trip, Bob and Paul also meet Mick May and Marina Gibson, who together have started a charity called Cancer and Pisces, which offers fishing as therapeutic respite for people with cancer.

programme.desc: Kicking off the series in Buddy’s den, the gloves are on as Buddy and Conker are joined by Jackson, a young boxer who wants to learn a recipe that can pack a punch to keep his energy up! Buddy knows that Jackson loves a big-stacked sandwich, so what better than a homemade fish finger sandwich topped with crunchy lettuce and a simple, delicious, two-ingredient sauce, all packed into a soft bun?! Learning to cook means that you can make your meals exactly how you like them, so Jackson chooses cod and Buddy uses salmon, and things get messy when they breadcrumb the fish! Taking time out from the kitchen, Buddy is kept on his toes by Jackson as he gives him a lesson in boxing. Buddy learns to be light on his feet, throw a punch and read his opponent... Join Buddy, Conker and Jackson in this tasty episode of Cooking Buddies that certainly packs a punch! You can get all of Buddy’s recipes and LOADS more at bbc.co.uk/food

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos find themselves in an office. A man is shown in, and he has a good look around. He spins the office chair round and round. The manager comes in and they both sit down. The Twirlywoos spin the man's chair round and round. Then they spin the manager round and round. Eventually they are both spinning round and round whilst trying to conduct an interview! Back in the Big Red Boat it is time for fruit tea. The Fruit Tea Machine is malfunctioning. Great BigHoo tries to get the teapot under the spout but it is spinning round and round. Chickedy and Chick jump up to the spout and they spin round and round too! Toodloo and Great BigHoo join in and they all spin round and round on the spout.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Sullivan, Araiya, River, Taiba, Luna and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their little ones at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Nigel has got a shopping basket inside his bag. All the parents and babies have different objects and toys that are themed around a trip to the shops too, which are explored through play, songs and a story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to hide a baby-appropriate shopping-themed toy or object inside a fabric bag or pillowcase, to discover with their baby! Some viewers at home show how they’ve been exploring shopping too. The fun children’s song Shopping Day features, as does a story about Baby Bear at the shops. The Baby Bear Song gets everyone moving about before some calm time with sensory lights and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children build a pretend sleepover den, learn British Sign Language signs for brother, sleeping and morning, then sing and sign Frère Jacques.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Aaron, Mia and Jackson go on a splishy-splashy mission to water the garden and discover how plants drink, with help from Chatterpot, colourful experiments and clever roots!

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Baby elephant Kipekee learns how to get rid of some buzzy flies with the help of her friends. Ranger Hamza spots lions in the wild and has fun playing with the baby rhinos.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the Pea-Rexes lose their ball near sleeping Cucumberdiles. A quiet retrieval fails.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: When Bingo stops playing Bluey’s spy game in the park, their device to control the grown-ups stops working properly! Bluey now sees how important Bingo is and needs to win her back!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee decides to make an omelette, but there are no eggs in the basket. Where are all the chickens, and why aren't they laying any eggs? The chickens need some exercise! Thank goodness for Hennie the ostrich and her exercise fitness. Watch the Squirrels work out with the chickens to Hennie's funky tunes.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Fun Pink arrives in Colourland. Learn about the colour pink with the Colourblocks!

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Jessie finds out all about some very speedy teeny tiny creatures – lizards. Chantelle joins Tom and Harvey to discover what lizards eat. Meanwhile, Rory and his son Sandy are at a country park trying to find the super speedy creatures who are very good at hiding. Chantelle and Rory’s fact files explain the differences between lizards and newts, how big lizards grow and which species can change colour. It’s also time to find out how lizards help the planet as predators. This episode’s Teeny Tiny Task is to make some great lizard art.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Kyra and Khloe plan a visit to Nana and make chocolate crispy cakes to surprise her with. Visiting Nana is a special occasion, so Mum draws pretty patterns on Kyra and Khloe’s hands using henna. At Nana’s they have a delicious picnic in the garden and then rescue a worm! But will Nana enjoy the cakes? And will the worm be alright?

programme.title: Big Cook Little Cook
programme.desc: Jen amazes Small with her tap-dancing skills. Small finds out how ginger is grown and ground. Plus, the two chefs cheer up a lonely gingerbread man with some gingerbread friends.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Kika is a golden labrador and guide dog for her owner Dr Amit, who is blind, which means he cannot see. She is trained to use her supersight to help Dr Amit do as many things as he can by himself. Together, they make the best team! Dr Amit is helping Raj the grocer judge the carrots in the fruit and veg competition at the Woofton country fair. Kika is helping Dr Amit, including with the mouthwatering task of finding the tastiest carrot in Woofton! But when Amit has to bring the prize-winning carrots to the photographer from the Woofton Gazette, Kika must guide Amit safely back through the maze of stalls, visitors and obstacles while carrying a precious carrot cargo.

programme.title: Time for School
programme.desc: It’s Silas and his classmates' first full day at school! There are lots of things to explore, new friends to make and teachers to meet. After meeting the teachers, the children explore the classroom and outdoor area. At lunchtime, Ottilie and Bryn ‘spot’ an invisible mouse in the dining hall. Lusungu finds that opening yogurt lids can be a bit tricky. Luckily, Mrs Farrell is on hand to help. The day continues as Silas and Maily create family portraits. Silas has fun drawing his mum's, but finds it harder to draw his pet cats - so he draws rabbits instead!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Isabelle, Phoenix and Oona are on their way to meet Mossy. Baba and Lala want to come too! When the older pufflings get distracted, Baba takes Lala under his little wing - but she wanders off. Baba searches all over for her. When he finds Lala in Flynne's den, Baba proves he can take care of himself now - and Lala too!

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Lu's upset when Declan takes a bite of her pear.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: It’s almost bedtime, but Maddie doesn’t want to brush her teeth. Dad tells her all about the mysterious pearly whites (aka her teeth!), and how they sometimes start to sing when they’re tickled. Really, singing teeth? It couldn’t be true… Could it?

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Charlie has made a huge pie for the Piggies to share! But Wilf wants it all for himself and sabotages his own house to trap the Piggies outside. While they fix his home, Wilf settles in theirs... until the Piggies rush back to save their pie party!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: When Five and friends go missing from the five-star ball, Six to Ten discover they are all Five-and-a-friend! Learn about splitting numbers into smaller numbers with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Educational series using Makaton sign language. Mr Tumble helps Grandad Tumble water his vegetables, and Justin and his friends have fun gardening and making a scarecrow.

programme.title: Teletubbies

programme.title: Andy's Prehistoric Adventures
programme.desc: Andy travels back 95 million years in search of an eggshell belonging to one of the biggest animals to ever walk the earth.

programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s Stall. She chooses the pencil drumsticks and remembers the day she got them. Mack is in charge of the Kids Club, and the children are all creating cool drawings for Molly who has been off with chickenpox and feeling a little fed up. Molly’s friends try to think about what they could do to cheer her up when Eilidh has an idea. Mack could write a song for Molly, and they could sing it to her when they video call her later. As Daisy arrives to help out, Mack suggests that the kids make their own instruments to play along, while he goes to write the song. Unfortunately, Mack tries so hard to write the perfect song that he runs out of time. Can the kids come to Mack’s rescue?

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this episode, CBeebies’ very own motorcycle rider, Grace, shows off three amazing machines that are all made for people with disabilities. With the help of Talan Skeels-Piggins, Grace races a superbike for disabled riders, shows off the amazing handcycle and takes a mobility car for a spin.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: It's the first day of Pup School. Dodge overcomes his first day nerves as he meets lots of new friends. The pups settle into their class activities with their new teacher Miss Collie.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger discovers some unexpected guests hiding in her tail - three baby Pea-Rexes.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: A Malabar squirrel stuck aboard the Octoray starts to build stashes all over the ship.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Peter, Benjamin and Lily are tempted by a mysterious hoard of radishes, Lily finds herself caught in Mr Tod's trap. Can Peter find a way to rescue Lily before Mr Tod reaches her?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels have played with all their toys, and they are frustrated because they feel they have nothing left to do. Duggee tells them that there’s always limitless fun if you use your imagination. He explains that you can use your mind to pretend to do or be anything you want and demonstrates how he can imagine he’s a dancer or even a horse. The Squirrels take turns thinking of what they want to be or what they want to do. At first, not everyone gets the hang of it, but soon enough, they all embark on their greatest adventure yet, in the new world they have imagined. Together, they can speed through space or float through an underwater world, where Norrie is a rock star and Tag can be king. All that immersive fun can happen just from the clubhouse!

Her feet become bouncy, and it's brilliant at first, until she realises that bouncing everywhere makes simple jobs tricky. Rafi doesn’t want any help, but soon she sees that bouncing all the time isn’t as fun as she thought. With her dads' support, she realises it’s okay to ask for help. Together, they share pancakes, laughter and a big upside-down hug.

programme.desc: Tiny and her flower friends are playing a lovely tune with the music trees when suddenly they hear a strange voice joining in - it seems to be coming from high in the sky. On investigation, Tiny discovers a lone flower singing as she travels alone through space on a rocky asteroid. Tiny discovers that the flower is lonely and comes up with a clever plan to help her.

programme.desc: MeMo loves jumping, but BaBa is struggling to jump like MeMo. At the Play Tree, they play with a jumpy planet that can jump very high. On the Lullaby Lake, Fungi and Pungi jump out of the water to greet MeMo and BaBa as they make their way to Gramma Leeba in the Bay of Books.

The Baby Bear Song gets everyone moving about before some calm time with sensory lights and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children build a pretend sleepover den, learn British Sign Language signs for brother, sleeping and morning, then sing and sign Frère Jacques.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Aaron, Mia and Jackson go on a splishy-splashy mission to water the garden and discover how plants drink, with help from Chatterpot, colourful experiments and clever roots!

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Baby elephant Kipekee learns how to get rid of some buzzy flies with the help of her friends. Ranger Hamza spots lions in the wild and has fun playing with the baby rhinos.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the Pea-Rexes lose their ball near sleeping Cucumberdiles. A quiet retrieval fails.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: When Bingo stops playing Bluey’s spy game in the park, their device to control the grown-ups stops working properly! Bluey now sees how important Bingo is and needs to win her back!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee decides to make an omelette, but there are no eggs in the basket. Where are all the chickens, and why aren't they laying any eggs? The chickens need some exercise! Thank goodness for Hennie the ostrich and her exercise fitness. Watch the Squirrels work out with the chickens to Hennie's funky tunes.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Fun Pink arrives in Colourland. Learn about the colour pink with the Colourblocks!

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Jessie finds out all about some very speedy teeny tiny creatures – lizards. Chantelle joins Tom and Harvey to discover what lizards eat. Meanwhile, Rory and his son Sandy are at a country park trying to find the super speedy creatures who are very good at hiding. Chantelle and Rory’s fact files explain the differences between lizards and newts, how big lizards grow and which species can change colour. It’s also time to find out how lizards help the planet as predators. This episode’s Teeny Tiny Task is to make some great lizard art.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Kyra and Khloe plan a visit to Nana and make chocolate crispy cakes to surprise her with. Visiting Nana is a special occasion, so Mum draws pretty patterns on Kyra and Khloe’s hands using henna. At Nana’s they have a delicious picnic in the garden and then rescue a worm! But will Nana enjoy the cakes? And will the worm be alright?

programme.title: Big Cook Little Cook
programme.desc: Jen amazes Small with her tap-dancing skills. Small finds out how ginger is grown and ground. Plus, the two chefs cheer up a lonely gingerbread man with some gingerbread friends.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Kika is a golden labrador and guide dog for her owner Dr Amit, who is blind, which means he cannot see. She is trained to use her supersight to help Dr Amit do as many things as he can by himself. Together, they make the best team! Dr Amit is helping Raj the grocer judge the carrots in the fruit and veg competition at the Woofton country fair. Kika is helping Dr Amit, including with the mouthwatering task of finding the tastiest carrot in Woofton! But when Amit has to bring the prize-winning carrots to the photographer from the Woofton Gazette, Kika must guide Amit safely back through the maze of stalls, visitors and obstacles while carrying a precious carrot cargo.

programme.title: Time for School
programme.desc: It’s Silas and his classmates' first full day at school! There are lots of things to explore, new friends to make and teachers to meet. After meeting the teachers, the children explore the classroom and outdoor area. At lunchtime, Ottilie and Bryn ‘spot’ an invisible mouse in the dining hall. Lusungu finds that opening yogurt lids can be a bit tricky. Luckily, Mrs Farrell is on hand to help. The day continues as Silas and Maily create family portraits. Silas has fun drawing his mum's, but finds it harder to draw his pet cats - so he draws rabbits instead!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Isabelle, Phoenix and Oona are on their way to meet Mossy. Baba and Lala want to come too! When the older pufflings get distracted, Baba takes Lala under his little wing - but she wanders off. Baba searches all over for her. When he finds Lala in Flynne's den, Baba proves he can take care of himself now - and Lala too!

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Lu's upset when Declan takes a bite of her pear.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: It’s almost bedtime, but Maddie doesn’t want to brush her teeth. Dad tells her all about the mysterious pearly whites (aka her teeth!), and how they sometimes start to sing when they’re tickled. Really, singing teeth? It couldn’t be true… Could it?

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: Charlie has made a huge pie for the Piggies to share! But Wilf wants it all for himself and sabotages his own house to trap the Piggies outside. While they fix his home, Wilf settles in theirs... until the Piggies rush back to save their pie party!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: When Five and friends go missing from the five-star ball, Six to Ten discover they are all Five-and-a-friend! Learn about splitting numbers into smaller numbers with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: J is convinced she's a jaybird - but she just can't seem to fly. V makes a van and soon they are on a musical road trip to find the friends who can help J reach for the sky. This episode introduces the letters J and V and the words van, jog, jig, jug, vet and jet.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Educational series using Makaton sign language. Mr Tumble helps Grandad Tumble water his vegetables, and Justin and his friends have fun gardening and making a scarecrow.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Tubby Custard Machine is making tubby custard bubbles - lots and lots of them! The Teletubbies have fun chasing and popping the bubbles, just like the children in Tummy Tales.

programme.title: Andy's Prehistoric Adventures
programme.desc: Andy travels back 95 million years in search of an eggshell belonging to one of the biggest animals to ever walk the earth.

programme.title: Molly and Mack
programme.desc: Molly examines her shelf of special things at the back of Mack’s Stall. She chooses the pencil drumsticks and remembers the day she got them. Mack is in charge of the Kids Club, and the children are all creating cool drawings for Molly who has been off with chickenpox and feeling a little fed up. Molly’s friends try to think about what they could do to cheer her up when Eilidh has an idea. Mack could write a song for Molly, and they could sing it to her when they video call her later. As Daisy arrives to help out, Mack suggests that the kids make their own instruments to play along, while he goes to write the song. Unfortunately, Mack tries so hard to write the perfect song that he runs out of time. Can the kids come to Mack’s rescue?

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this episode, CBeebies’ very own motorcycle rider, Grace, shows off three amazing machines that are all made for people with disabilities. With the help of Talan Skeels-Piggins, Grace races a superbike for disabled riders, shows off the amazing handcycle and takes a mobility car for a spin.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: It's the first day of Pup School. Dodge overcomes his first day nerves as he meets lots of new friends. The pups settle into their class activities with their new teacher Miss Collie.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger discovers some unexpected guests hiding in her tail - three baby Pea-Rexes.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: A Malabar squirrel stuck aboard the Octoray starts to build stashes all over the ship.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Peter, Benjamin and Lily are tempted by a mysterious hoard of radishes, Lily finds herself caught in Mr Tod's trap. Can Peter find a way to rescue Lily before Mr Tod reaches her?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels have played with all their toys, and they are frustrated because they feel they have nothing left to do. Duggee tells them that there’s always limitless fun if you use your imagination. He explains that you can use your mind to pretend to do or be anything you want and demonstrates how he can imagine he’s a dancer or even a horse. The Squirrels take turns thinking of what they want to be or what they want to do. At first, not everyone gets the hang of it, but soon enough, they all embark on their greatest adventure yet, in the new world they have imagined. Together, they can speed through space or float through an underwater world, where Norrie is a rock star and Tag can be king. All that immersive fun can happen just from the clubhouse!

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Fergie is feeling off, Vida diagnoses her - she's having a sad day. It happens to everyone, and all she needs to do is take care of herself. Luckily, she has lots of friends to help out.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Supertato’s Tato belt gets locked inside a glass case for an exhibition, but Tomato can’t remember the code to get it out again, and Supertato needs it back to defeat Evil Pea.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: Weasy can't help but play rock music when he forms a band with the Ducklings, but it isn't their style. They ask him to leave the band - so he finds an electric guitar and plans to take over the show!

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Mojo and Bo have to make sure Dot doesn’t see her present before her birthday party. But that’s easier said than done when Dot becomes an unstoppable present-hunting machine.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey teaches Bingo how to use magic so she can make Mum play with her.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bingo must learn how to play by herself. Luckily, Dad has a problem that needs solving.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Feeling unappreciated, Gadabout discovers a talent for gardening. Zog and Pearl discover his green fingers have upset the natural balance of the land, making others ill.

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Elvis is torn between staying in goal or playing outfield. He excels at both but misses goalkeeping. Lucy aims to be the first to nutmeg Georgie, who has never been nutmegged before.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: The Brooklyn-Bells spend their first night together as a new family, only to be kept awake by Waffle, whose constant barking upsets Mrs Hobbs, their cat-obsessed neighbour.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi loves bouncing on the trampoline and wishes she could do it all day. Her feet become bouncy, and it's brilliant at first, until she realises that bouncing everywhere makes simple jobs tricky. Rafi doesn’t want any help, but soon she sees that bouncing all the time isn’t as fun as she thought. With her dads' support, she realises it’s okay to ask for help. Together, they share pancakes, laughter and a big upside-down hug.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: After going strawberry picking at the local strawberry farm, JoJo and Gran Gran have lots of juicy strawberries left over. They're too full to eat them, but Gran Gran has a plan! JoJo helps Gran Gran make delicious strawberry jam, which preserves the strawberries for a long time to come - meaning they can enjoy them over and over again.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. John has a problem with the origami flamingos he has made and needs Sarah and Duck's help.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Tiny and her flower friends are playing a lovely tune with the music trees when suddenly they hear a strange voice joining in - it seems to be coming from high in the sky. On investigation, Tiny discovers a lone flower singing as she travels alone through space on a rocky asteroid. Tiny discovers that the flower is lonely and comes up with a clever plan to help her.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo loves jumping, but BaBa is struggling to jump like MeMo. At the Play Tree, they play with a jumpy planet that can jump very high. BaBa uses the jumpy planet to jump - just like MeMo. The Yummies use the jumpy planet to collect raspberries for their snack. On the Lullaby Lake, Fungi and Pungi jump out of the water to greet MeMo and BaBa as they make their way to Gramma Leeba in the Bay of Books.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: Upsy Daisy is asleep in her bed when the ball bounces into the garden. While Upsy Daisy plays with the ball, Igglepiggle decides to go to sleep in Upsy Daisy's bed. This is not a wise move, as only Upsy Daisy is allowed to sleep in Upsy Daisy's bed. Upsy Daisy discovers Igglepiggle and chases him round and round. What will happen when Upsy Daisy leaves her bed to play with the ball again?

programme.desc: Mo Gilligan reads a funny Bedtime Story about a very hairy and very bear-y dad!

programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. Normandy is peppered with orchards and dairy farms, famed as cider and calvados country, and is also home to rich and world-famous butter - James sets up his mobile kitchen in one of the many apple orchards in the area, where he prepares a dish of artichokes with hollandaise. James also meets Laurent, who gave up working in a factory to make butter the way his mum taught him, and visits the Le Pave d'Auge restaurant in one of the most beautiful towns in France, where he meets a chef who likes to cook with as much butter as he does and is served a dish of sweetbreads and salsify. James then uses calvados in a pork dish with wet walnuts - All of this inspires two indulgent dishes back home, pain au chocolat using lots of that lovely butter, and black pudding with scallops.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. Normandy is peppered with orchards and dairy farms, famed as cider and calvados country, and is also home to rich and world-famous butter - James sets up his mobile kitchen in one of the many apple orchards in the area, where he prepares a dish of artichokes with hollandaise. James also meets Laurent, who gave up working in a factory to make butter the way his mum taught him, and visits the Le Pave d'Auge restaurant in one of the most beautiful towns in France, where he meets a chef who likes to cook with as much butter as he does and is served a dish of sweetbreads and salsify. James then uses calvados in a pork dish with wet walnuts - All of this inspires two indulgent dishes back home, pain au chocolat using lots of that lovely butter, and black pudding with scallops.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. Normandy is peppered with orchards and dairy farms, famed as cider and calvados country, and is also home to rich and world-famous butter - James sets up his mobile kitchen in one of the many apple orchards in the area, where he prepares a dish of artichokes with hollandaise. James also meets Laurent, who gave up working in a factory to make butter the way his mum taught him, and visits the Le Pave d'Auge restaurant in one of the most beautiful towns in France, where he meets a chef who likes to cook with as much butter as he does and is served a dish of sweetbreads and salsify. James then uses calvados in a pork dish with wet walnuts - All of this inspires two indulgent dishes back home, pain au chocolat using lots of that lovely butter, and black pudding with scallops.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. Normandy is peppered with orchards and dairy farms, famed as cider and calvados country, and is also home to rich and world-famous butter - James sets up his mobile kitchen in one of the many apple orchards in the area, where he prepares a dish of artichokes with hollandaise. James also meets Laurent, who gave up working in a factory to make butter the way his mum taught him, and visits the Le Pave d'Auge restaurant in one of the most beautiful towns in France, where he meets a chef who likes to cook with as much butter as he does and is served a dish of sweetbreads and salsify. James then uses calvados in a pork dish with wet walnuts - All of this inspires two indulgent dishes back home, pain au chocolat using lots of that lovely butter, and black pudding with scallops.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. Normandy is peppered with orchards and dairy farms, famed as cider and calvados country, and is also home to rich and world-famous butter - James sets up his mobile kitchen in one of the many apple orchards in the area, where he prepares a dish of artichokes with hollandaise. James also meets Laurent, who gave up working in a factory to make butter the way his mum taught him, and visits the Le Pave d'Auge restaurant in one of the most beautiful towns in France, where he meets a chef who likes to cook with as much butter as he does and is served a dish of sweetbreads and salsify. James then uses calvados in a pork dish with wet walnuts - All of this inspires two indulgent dishes back home, pain au chocolat using lots of that lovely butter, and black pudding with scallops.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. Normandy is peppered with orchards and dairy farms, famed as cider and calvados country, and is also home to rich and world-famous butter - James sets up his mobile kitchen in one of the many apple orchards in the area, where he prepares a dish of artichokes with hollandaise. James also meets Laurent, who gave up working in a factory to make butter the way his mum taught him, and visits the Le Pave d'Auge restaurant in one of the most beautiful towns in France, where he meets a chef who likes to cook with as much butter as he does and is served a dish of sweetbreads and salsify. James then uses calvados in a pork dish with wet walnuts - All of this inspires two indulgent dishes back home, pain au chocolat using lots of that lovely butter, and black pudding with scallops.

programme.title: The Only Way is Essex
programme.desc: Amy's attempt to mediate between her cousin Harry and new pal Bobby ended in a row at the curry house that got more heated than her vindaloo - now Bobby's not just got beef with Harry, but Amy too. Beneath the rivalry, old wounds surface as Pat reveals abandoned dance dreams, a pregnancy that ended her career, and her belief Mary betrayed her. Backstage, Mary and Pat discover the betrayal never happened and finally heal.

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: James's journey takes him to Pegasus Bridge - famous for the D-Day landings - which he drives across in his beloved 2CV. Normandy is peppered with orchards and dairy farms, famed as cider and calvados country, and is also home to rich and world-famous butter - James sets up his mobile kitchen in one of the many apple orchards in the area, where he prepares a dish of artichokes with hollandaise. James also meets Laurent, who gave up working in a factory to make butter the way his mum taught him, and visits the Le Pave d'Auge restaurant in one of the most beautiful towns in France, where he meets a chef who likes to cook with as much butter as he does and is served a dish of sweetbreads and salsify. James then uses calvados in a pork dish with wet walnuts - All of this inspires two indulgent dishes back home, pain au chocolat using lots of that lovely butter, and black pudding with scallops.

programme.title: Long Lost Family
programme.desc: The first episode in the 14th series of the show follows a mother who was forced to give up her daughter as she searches for her only child and an adopted woman looks for the brother who was separated from her as a baby - in our first case, Ros Webb was 16 years old when she discovered that she was pregnant and her strict parents made her travel 100 miles to London to hide her pregnancy and then give up her child for adoption. Her daughter Christine was the only child Ros ever had and she is desperate to reunite with her after 59 years - Long Lost Family also search on behalf of Tegan Cornish who had a difficult adoption. Tegan began to look for her birth family as an adult - when she ordered up her birth records, she was shocked to discover that she had a younger brother and even more surprised to discover that her brother was originally meant to be adopted with her but for some reason was separated from her and sent back into care.

In a case that has drawn millions of views on TikTok, 17-year-old Charlie Cosser was fatally stabbed by 16-year-old Yura Varybrus at an end-of-term summer party for teenagers - Charlie didn't know Yura but had asked him to leave after a girl said that he had been bothering her.
